title: OKR Roadmap Flywheel and Initiative De-risking Playbook
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description: Create a repeatable playbook that turns company-level OKRs into a 90-day roadmap flywheel with explicit de-risking gates for cross-functional initiatives. The playbook will define: (1) how to surface signals from quarterly metrics and product telemetry into initiative prioritization, (2) gating criteria and mitigation steps for high-risk initiatives before they enter committed delivery lanes, and (3) a lightweight cadence for continuous re-evaluation (weekly signal reviews, monthly re-scoping, and mid-quarter debriefs). Goal: reduce initiative rollback and scope churn by 30% and increase on-time delivery of OKR-linked milestones by 20% across eng/design/reliability teams.
acceptance_criteria: A documented playbook (Confluence) with step-by-step cadence and templates for: signal intake, risk scoring, de-risking checklist, and go/no-go gating
A prioritized checklist that program managers can use to move an initiative from Triage -> Committed with mandatory artifacts (risk matrix, e2e flow, SLO impacts, infra estimate)
Integration with existing roadmap board: new initiative states and tags implemented in Linear and surfaced to Console roadmap dashboard
Two pilot initiatives (one infra-heavy, one customer-facing) run through the playbook during Cycle 2026-W12 with post-mortem notes and quantitative metrics showing reduced rework
Runbook for escalation that includes named contacts in Eng/Infra/Legal and a simple rollback policy with cost thresholds
stakeholders: Sofia Alvarez - Head of Product Strategy
decisions: Adopt a 3-tier risk score (Low/Med/High) combining technical complexity, external dependency count, and SLO exposure
Require high-risk initiatives to complete a lightweight technical spike and an infra cost estimate before being marked Committed
Use Linear workflow states (Triage -> Scoped -> De-risking -> Committed -> Active -> At-Risk -> Done) to make risk explicit on the roadmap
Keep playbook lightweight: no more than 5 mandatory artifacts to avoid blocking small but high-value initiatives

risks: Playbook becomes an extra gating bureaucracy if templates are too heavy — mitigate by limiting mandatory artifacts to 5
Insufficient data signals lead to noise in prioritization — mitigate by curating 6 leading indicators and instrumenting them before pilots
Cross-functional ownership gaps: initiatives stall when no single owner is accountable — mitigate by enforcing a named RACI entry before Committed state
Tooling gap: Linear states need minimal custom automation to avoid manual tagging drift — engineering dependency scheduled (ENG-4021)
